title: Log swallowed exceptions in profiles' log-less catch blocks instead of silently discarding them

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
      // no-op: cloud push failure is non-fatal; local write already succeeded (offline-first)

why: Five catch blocks across this batch swallow exceptions with zero AppLogger call — three in profile_repository_impl.dart discard cloud-sync push failures (create/update/self-heal) with only a code comment, and two more (profile_picker_screen.dart, add_profile_dialog.dart) silently clear a live duplicate-name validation error on any DB exception. add_profile_dialog.dart's own line 269-280 shows the correct pattern (AppLogger.instance.error with event/exception/stackTrace) right next to one of the log-less ones, proving the gap is an oversight, not a style choice. Without logging, a real production failure pattern (e.g. outbox writes silently failing on a subset of devices) leaves no telemetry trail to diagnose from.
recommendation: Replace each `catch (_) { ... }` with a catch that logs via AppLogger.instance.warning/error (event + exception) before continuing with the existing non-fatal behavior.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 listed catch blocks call AppLogger before continuing
A grep-based Rule-0 check (or custom_lint rule, once custom_lint is unblocked) flags `catch (_) {` / `catch (e) {` blocks in lib/ with no AppLogger call in their body

corrections: Digest posture #3 explicitly names 'log-less catch' as its own canonical P3/minimal example ('naming drift, missing const, log-less catch, a 401-line file'). This finding is exactly that archetype at 5 sites — P2 is an inflation relative to the digest's own calibration; lowering to P3.
